title: The Low-Carbon Development Strategy of Russia Until 2050 and the Role of Forests in Its Implementation
content: The article examines the role of managed ecosystems, and particularly forests in achieving carbon neutrality in Russia. The range of estimates of Russia’s forests’ net carbon balance in different studies [8, 11, 43] is presented. The comparison of Russia National GHG inventory 2023 and 2024 data is presented and explained. The possible changes in Russia Long term Low-emission Development Strategy of Russia (LT LEDS) carbon neutrality scenario due to new land use, land-use change and forestry (LULUCF) data in National GHG Inventory Document (NID) 2024 are discussed. The assessment of changes in the drafts of the Operational plan of the LT LEDS is presented, it is concluded that its structure and content has significantly improved. The article highlights the problem of GHG emissions from forest fires and compares official “ground based” and Remote Sensing approaches in calculation of such emissions. Taking into account the intention to increase net absorption by implementing forest carbon projects, the latest changes in regulation of such projects is discussed. The estimates of GHG potential of forest related carbon projects are provided. Proposals are presented for the development of the national forest policy towards increasing net forest carbon absorption, including considering the projected decrease in annual net absorption by Russian forests by 2050. The latest changes in the legal regulation of forest climate projects are presented. Var-ious options for calculating the potential for the implementation of ecosystem climate projects in Russia are presented, considering the limitation of the cost of carbon units and the full potential.
